info.title: BlackBox HFT API
info.description: Research-only simulated execution forensics. Every nanosecond quantity (`*_ns`, `ts`, `*_ts`) and every seed is a decimal string. Errors use the envelope `ErrorEnvelope`. See docs/engineering/API_CONTRACT.md.

get.summary: Everything that happened in a window, for the timeline view, cursor-paged over its events.
get.description:
Events are paged in tape `seq` order (a stable unique key, so equal timestamps never split
or repeat across pages); follow `next_cursor` until it is `null` to get every event counted
by `events_total`. A page holds at most `max_events` events and fits the caller's response
cap (anonymous: 1 MiB): it ends early with `truncated_by = "bytes"` instead of failing.
`fills`, `equity` and `orders` are sent on the first page (no `cursor`) only and are empty
on `cursor` pages; when they alone exceed the cap the request is refused with 400
`invalid_request` (`details.reason = "window_too_large"`): request a shorter window.

parameters.name: t0_ns
parameters.description: Inclusive window start (default: run start).

parameters.name: t1_ns
parameters.description: Inclusive window end (default: `min(run end, t0 + 60 s)`).

parameters.name: max_events
cursor
parameters.description: `next_cursor` of the previous page; `t0_ns`, `t1_ns` and `platform` must be unchanged.

oneOf.description:
The earliest non-identical pair in decision order (tick, slot). Every pair before it is
`identical`; everything after it may differ as a knock-on effect.

The earliest pair whose decision or fills differ (see [`PairClass::is_outcome_divergence`]).
Pairs before it may differ in timing, fees or recorded history, never in decision or fills.

pairs.description: Non-identical pairs in decision order, capped at `pairs_cap`.

allOf.description: Probability of Backtest Overfitting by CSCV.

blocks.description: `S`: equal time blocks of the selection window.

cells.description: `N`: configurations in the matrix (all declared cells).

pbo.description:
Fraction of the train/test splits in which the in-sample best ranks at or below the
out-of-sample median (logit ≤ 0).

Availability_Pbo.description: A statistic, or the reason it is not reported.

spearman_rho.description: Spearman's rho between in-sample and out-of-sample values (average ranks for ties).

Availability_RankCorrelation.description: A statistic, or the reason it is not reported.

horizon_s.description: Remaining horizon `T - t` in seconds, held constant (the common stationary variant).

kappa.description: Order-arrival decay `kappa` (per price unit) in `lambda(delta) = A * exp(-kappa * delta)`.

vol_halflife_ticks.description: Volatility is an exponentially weighted estimate of mid-price changes with this half-life.

Basis.description: How strongly a statement in an explanation is supported.

BboSeries.description:
Top of book at every change, columnar. `bid_tick[i]`/`ask_tick[i]` hold from `ts[i]` until
`ts[i + 1]`.

bid_tick.description: `None` while that side of the reconstructed book is empty.

CalibrationSampling.description: Sampling used to estimate the discrete Stoikov chain; distinct from report display sampling.

Caveat.description: A plain-language warning that belongs next to the numbers.

oneOf.description: `None` when `eligibility.aligned` is false: order ids would not name the same decisions.

interpretation.description: Supported and unsupported readings of the difference.

metrics.description: Returned even when `eligibility.like_for_like` is false; they are then not like-for-like.

ConfigDiff.description: One configuration field that differs between two runs.

path.description: Dotted path into the serialized [`RunConfig`], e.g. `execution.order_latency.entry_ns`.

missing.description:
Cells with neither an in-sample value nor an error (not run, cancelled, or the objective
undefined for them).

tried.description:
Every configuration the spec declares. All of them count as trials for selection bias,
whether they completed, failed or never ran.

platform.description: Platform class of both runs (default: this deployment's result platform).

CubicLeg.description: One leg of the `heavy_tail` (ABIDES cubic) latency model.

clip.description:
ABIDES `jitter_clip`: `x` is drawn from `(clip, 1]`. Must be in `(0, 1)`; it bounds the
largest latency at `min + jitter * min / (unit * clip^3)`.

jitter.description: ABIDES `jitter` (`a`): shape of the cubic curve, in `[0, 1]`.

min_ns.description: Minimum latency in ns; also the scale of the jitter.

unit.description: ABIDES `jitter_unit`: the jitter is measured in units of `min / unit`.

DataLevel.description: Level of market data the dataset actually contains. Never overstated.

DatasetManifest.description: Persisted next to the event file as `dataset.json`.

events_file.description: File name of the engine event array inside the dataset directory.

events_sha256.description: SHA-256 of that file. This is the dataset hash recorded in run manifests.

generator.description: For synthetic datasets, the exact generator configuration (so it can be regenerated).

origin_ns.description:
Absolute epoch nanoseconds of the dataset origin (its first exchange timestamp), as a
decimal string. All `RelNs` values for this dataset are relative to it.

DecisionOutcome.description: What one scenario did with a decision.

terminal_ts.description: Exchange clock: when the order became terminal (its completion).

DeltaStats.description: Distribution of one timing delta (B minus A, nanoseconds) over the pairs that have it.

count.description: Pairs where both orders have the timestamp.

median.description: Mean of the two middle values when `count` is even.

nonzero.description: Of those, pairs where the delta is not zero.

run_id.description: The visible run for this exact configuration, if it has been simulated.

DepthFrame.description:
The reconstructed book at one instant: up to `levels` price levels per side, best first, as
`(price_tick, qty)`.

Dispersion.description: Spread of one set of cell values (raw metric values, not oriented).

p25.description: Quantiles by linear interpolation between order statistics (Hyndman & Fan type 7).

std_dev.description: Sample standard deviation (n − 1); `None` for one value.

DownsampledSeries.description: One series shortened in an analytics response.

path.description:
JSON Pointer of the series in the report, e.g. `/execution/first_fill/km/curve`; pass it
as `path` to the series endpoint.

Eligibility.description:
Whether two runs can be compared order by order and like for like. Checked before any
per-order alignment.

aligned.description: Per-order alignment was produced: no reason has [`EligibilityEffect::NoAlignment`].

like_for_like.description:
No reason at all: metric deltas compare the same market, instrument, strategy kind,
decision grid, sampling and simulator.

EligibilityEffect.description: What an eligibility difference does to a comparison.

EligibilityReason.description: One identity field that differs between the runs (or could not be verified).

a.description: The value in run A; `null` when unknown.

EngineStateCheck.description: Cross-check of BlackBox's own ledger against the engine's local-side account state.

agrees.description: Position, cash, fee and trade-count agreement at the end of the run.

note.description: Explains an expected disagreement (see docs/EXECUTION_MODEL.md), or is empty.

EnsembleMember.description: One seed of a segment and the run it produced.

run_id.description: The run's 16-hex id; `None` until it completed.

EnsembleReport.description: The report of one seed ensemble.

collapse_reason.description: The explicit statement of a collapse; `None` when the seeds differ.

collapsed.description:
Every seed produced the same result: by construction when `seed_affects_result` is
`false`, or observed (every segment `identical`).

seed_affects_result.description:
Whether the configuration's order-latency model uses the seed at all. `false` (constant
latency, or jitter of zero) means every seed replays the same simulation.

EnsembleSegment.description: The ensemble on one part of the data: the whole dataset, in sample or out of sample.

identical.description: At least two runs completed and all of them have exactly the same metrics.

members.description: Every seed, in the spec's order.

metrics.description: Every [`ObjectiveMetric`] defined for at least one completed run.

EquitySample.description: Periodic account snapshot on the local clock.

cash.description: Cumulative signed cash flow from fills, before fees.

known_position.description: Position the strategy knew about at `ts` (fill notifications received).

mid_tick.description: Local mid used for marking (fractional ticks). `None` until the local book has two sides.

position.description: Position from all simulated fills that have happened at the exchange by `ts`.

tick_no.description:
Strategy tick the sample was taken on. A run's last sample is its closing sample: it is
taken one interval after the final tick, once everything that followed that tick has been
processed, and carries `tick_no` equal to the number of ticks evaluated.

unrealized_pnl.description: `position * (mid - average entry price)`; 0 while flat or unmarked.

details.description: Code-specific structured details (API_CONTRACT §2); `null` when there are none.

rows.description:
Rows in the engine event array (a source row whose exchange and local order differ is
split into two rows, so this can exceed the sum of the others).

ExchangeModel.description: Which pinned-engine exchange model matches orders.

ExecutionConfig.description: The modeled execution assumptions. These are what counterfactual scenarios vary.

feed_latency_offset_ns.description:
Added to every feed event's local receipt time (engine `latency_offset`). Zero keeps the
dataset's own exchange-to-local latency. Must keep `local_ts > exch_ts` for every event.

think_time_ns.description:
Strategy compute ("think") time: requests decided on a tick are handed to the order path
this long after the decision (ABIDES "computation delay"). The decision itself uses only
what had arrived by the tick. Zero (the default, omitted from JSON) sends at the tick.
Must be below `strategy.interval_ns` so the decision grid does not move.

order_details_streamed.description: True when details were delivered to a sink rather than retained in `orders`.

oneOf.description: Detail only.

status.description:
`completed` when a run exists, else the job state, `cancelled` after this workspace
cancelled, or `detached`.

ExplainStep.description: One link in the chain of reasoning.

event_seqs.description: Tape `seq` values this statement rests on (possibly empty for `Unobservable` caveats).

statement.description: One or two plain sentences with concrete numbers.

caveats.description:
Limits of what this explanation can claim. Always includes that queue position on
Market-By-Price data is modeled and that replayed orders do not affect historical prices.

queue_path.description: Modeled quantity ahead over time (empty for orders that never rested).

FeeConfig.description:
Fees as a fraction of traded value (engine `TradingValueFeeModel<CommonFees>`). Negative means
a rebate. Example: `0.0002` is 2 basis points.

FillRecord.description: One simulated execution with its accounting effect.

markout_ticks.description:
Derived: `side.sign() * (mid(t + h) - price_tick)` in ticks for each horizon in
[`MARKOUT_HORIZONS_NS`]. Positive means the market moved in the fill's favour. `None` when
the dataset ends before the horizon or the book was not valid then.

mid_tick.description: Derived: mid price (fractional ticks) of the dataset's book at the fill's exchange time.

position_after.description: Position after this fill (all simulated fills up to here, exchange clock).

realized_pnl.description: Realized P&L booked by this fill under average-cost accounting, before fees.

seq.description: `seq` of the corresponding `ExchFill` on the tape.

oneOf.description: The strategy decided to place an order. Recorded before risk checks.

known_position.description: Position as known locally at the decision.

market.description: Market as known locally at the decision.

oneOf.description: The strategy decided to cancel an order.

A risk rule stopped an intent before it reached the engine. `order_id` is the id the order
would have had.
A run-level risk rule fired; the harness cancels working orders and stops placing new ones.

Clock::Local. The local side sent a request. `entry_latency_ns` is the modeled latency the
engine drew for it. A negative value is the engine's convention for "rejected before
reaching the matching engine"; then `exch_arrival_ts` is `None`.

exch_arrival_ts.description:
Scheduled arrival at the exchange (`ts + entry_latency_ns`). The engine's order bus
never lets a request overtake an earlier one, so actual processing can be later; the
exchange-clock events show when it really happened.

oneOf.description:
Clock::Local. The engine refused a request synchronously (for example a cancel while
another request for the same order is in flight). Nothing was sent.

Clock::Exchange. The exchange model accepted a limit order to rest and the queue model
initialised its position.

level_qty.description: Displayed quantity at the order's price at that moment (observed market data).

queue_ahead.description:
Modeled quantity ahead of the order. `None` only if the queue model's state could not
be read, which the recorder reports rather than guesses.

oneOf.description: Clock::Exchange. A trade or depth change at the order's price moved the queue estimate.

ahead_after.description:
Negative means the modeled queue ahead is exhausted by that much; the exchange model
turns this into a fill.

oneOf.description: Clock::Exchange. One simulated execution.

fee.description: Fee charged for this execution in quote currency (negative is a rebate).

maker.description: `true`: filled while resting. `false`: took liquidity on arrival.

oneOf.description: Clock::Exchange. The exchange emitted a response toward the local side.

local_arrival_ts.description: Scheduled local arrival. Same ordering caveat as `RequestSent::exch_arrival_ts`.

request_rejected.description:
The exchange rejected the request this responds to (a cancel for an order that no
longer exists there).

oneOf.description: Clock::Local. The local side received a response and updated its view of the order.

exch_ts.description: When the exchange produced this response.

exec_qty.description: Quantity of the execution this response reports (0 when it reports none).

oneOf.description:
The per-order cap on queue updates was reached; `dropped` updates that changed the estimate
by less than one lot were not kept after this point.

order_id.description: The order this event concerns. `None` for run-level events.

seq.description: Position on the tape, starting at 0, contiguous.

ts.description: When the event happened, in `clock`'s domain.

oneOf.description: Continuous uniform on `[min, max)`.

GlftParams.description:
Guéant-Lehalle-Fernandez-Tapia market maker (`crates/bb-strategies/src/glft.rs`). Units:
prices in price units, quantities in base units; `order_qty` is the trade size `Delta` of
Guéant (2017) and the inventory `q` is the locally known position, both in base units.

gamma.description:
Absolute risk aversion `gamma` of the CARA objective, per unit of wealth
(1 / (price unit x base unit)). `xi = gamma` (Guéant 2017, Model A).

intensity_a.description:
Intensity scale `A`: fills per second of a quote at the reference price. An assumption,
not estimated from the data.

kappa.description: Intensity decay `k` (per price unit) in `Lambda(delta) = A * exp(-k * delta)`.

max_position.description: Inventory bound `Q` (base units): a side is not quoted when one more fill would pass it.

order_qty.description: Quote size `Delta` (base units); also the trade size in the formulas.

sigma_source.description: Which observed price series `sigma` is estimated from.

vol_halflife_ticks.description: Half-life, in strategy ticks, of the exponentially weighted variance estimate.

oneOf.description:
Sets both entry and response order latency to each value: the location parameter of the
model (`OrderLatencyConfig::with_base_ns`), keeping jitter and shape parameters.
Sets only the entry latency (new orders and cancels), the same way.

GridAxis.description: A parameter swept along one axis of a sensitivity grid.

GridSpec.description: A bounded two-dimensional sweep around a base configuration.

matched_effective_half.description: Same valid cohort as RS and AS, allowing the identity to be checked after exclusions.

hold_ticks.description: Close the position this many strategy ticks after entry.

threshold.description: Enter when `(bid_qty - ask_qty) / (bid_qty + ask_qty)` exceeds this in absolute value.

name.description: File name or URL as supplied.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file exactly as read (compressed bytes for `.gz`).

InstrumentMeta.description: Static description of the traded instrument.

contract_size.description: Quote-currency value of `1.0` quantity at price `1.0` (1 for linear contracts).

lot_size.description: Minimum quantity increment in base units.

tick_size.description: Minimum price increment in quote currency.

oneOf.description: `min, min + step, …` up to and including `max` when it lies on the grid.

InterpretationNote.description: A statement about the comparison and how well it is supported.

Job.description:
API_CONTRACT §9.3. `running → queued` is a legal transition (re-queued after a drain or a
lost lease); `attempt` and `lease_losses` tell the two apart.

detached.description: Set by `POST /jobs/{id}/cancel` when only the caller's experiment was detached.

LatencyBreakdown.description:
Named time intervals of the order's life. Each is `None` when one of its endpoints never
occurred.

cancel_entry_latency_ns.description: Modeled entry latency of the cancel request.

feed_latency_ns.description:
Feed latency of that event: its local receipt minus its exchange time, including the
run's configured `feed_latency_offset_ns`. The dataset part is measured, synthetic or
assumed according to the dataset's provenance; the offset is always an assumption.

feed_staleness_ns.description:
Age of the market data the decision was based on: decision time minus the local receipt
time of the last feed event (local clock).

response_latency_ns.description: Modeled response latency of the first response.

resting_time_ns.description: Exchange clock: arrival to terminal state.

time_to_first_fill_ns.description: Exchange clock: arrival to first fill.

max_matched_trades.description: Bounds attribution bookkeeping even under an arbitrarily dense trade stream.

trade_match_lag_ns.description: Absolute exchange timestamp distance allowed for price-matched trade attribution.

LocalTsProvenance.description:
Where the local receipt timestamps came from. Decides whether feed latency may be presented as
measured.

LogNormalLeg.description: One leg of the `log_normal` latency model.

sigma.description: Standard deviation of `ln(latency)`. Zero makes the leg constant at the median.

bid_depth_truncated.description: True if any evaluated M3 band reaches beyond the deepest published level seen so far.

ofi_intervals.description: Bounded last-interval-per-time-bin view; total OFI above includes every transition.

trade_intervals.description: Same bounded interval-view policy as ofi_intervals.

MarketView.description: Top of book as the strategy host knew it, with the provenance of that knowledge.

best_bid_tick.description: `None` while the local book has no bid.

feed_exch_ts.description: Exchange timestamp of the last feed event received locally.

feed_local_ts.description: Local receipt timestamp of that event.

MarkoutStat.description: One markout horizon aggregated over fills.

fills.description: Fills for which the markout could be measured.

mean_ticks.description: Quantity-weighted mean markout in ticks. Negative means adverse selection.

MetricRow.description: One measured outcome side by side.

MetricSpread.description: Spread of one metric over the completed seeds of a segment.

std_dev.description: Sample standard deviation (n − 1); `None` below two values.

Metrics.description: Run-level measured outcomes. Every number is computed from the tape, fills and equity samples.

fill_ratio_orders.description: Orders with at least one fill divided by orders submitted.

fill_ratio_qty.description: Filled quantity divided by submitted quantity.

oneOf.description: Engine `ConstantLatency`.

BlackBox model implementing the engine's `LatencyModel` trait: the base latency plus a
seeded uniform draw from `[0, jitter_ns]`. The draw is a pure function of the seed and of
what is delayed (entry: order id and request time; response: exchange timestamp), never a
sequential stream, so results do not depend on the engine's internal iteration order. The
engine's order bus keeps messages in send order, so jitter never reorders them.

BlackBox model: every leg is an independent seeded log-normal draw
`median_ns * exp(sigma * Z)`, `Z ~ N(0, 1)`, keyed like `jitter`. `cancel` is the entry
distribution of cancel requests; `None` draws cancels from `entry`'s parameters (on the
cancel sub-stream).

BlackBox model: every leg is ABIDES' "cubic" latency, `min + (jitter / x^3) * (min / unit)`
with `x` uniform on `(clip, 1]` (abides-core `latency_model.py`). A clipped power-law
tail: rare messages are very slow. Keyed and sub-streamed like `log_normal`.

A market trade printed at the order's price. `qty` is the traded quantity.
The displayed quantity at the order's price changed from `prev_qty` to `new_qty`.

After a partial maker fill the engine's queue model puts the order's remainder at the
front of the queue (estimate reset to zero). Recorded directly after the `ExchFill` it
belongs to, and only when the order survives the fill.

QueueCause.description: The market event that moved a queue estimate.

oneOf.description:
Engine `RiskAdverseQueueModel`: the queue ahead shrinks only when trades print at the
order's price. Cancellations ahead are never credited. Most conservative.

Engine `ProbQueueModel<LogProbQueueFunc>`: a decrease in level quantity is split between
ahead and behind with `p(behind) = f(back) / (f(back) + f(front))`, `f(x) = ln(1 + x)`.

Engine `ProbQueueModel<LogProbQueueFunc2>`: `p(behind) = f(back) / f(back + front)`,
`f(x) = ln(1 + x)`.

Engine `ProbQueueModel<PowerProbQueueFunc>`: `f(x) = x^n`,
`p(behind) = f(back) / (f(back) + f(front))`.

Engine `ProbQueueModel<PowerProbQueueFunc2>`: `f(x) = x^n`,
`p(behind) = f(back) / f(back + front)`.
Engine `ProbQueueModel<PowerProbQueueFunc3>`: `p(behind) = 1 - (front / (front + back))^n`.

Once an order has this many updates, a depth-driven update is kept only if it moves the

oneOf.description:
Every combination of one or two axes. Cells are ordered row-major, the first axis
varying fastest: cell `yi * x_len + xi` (as in `GridResult`).

`samples` configurations drawn from the declared parameter domains with `seed`.

Combinations of the discrete parameters are drawn uniformly **without replacement**. When
`samples` exceeds the number of discrete combinations (possible only with a continuous
parameter), every combination is used once before any is used again. Continuous
parameters are drawn uniformly, each from its own seeded stream, so adding a parameter
never changes the values another one receives.

One configuration (`base`) replayed under several seeds: an ensemble that measures how
much of a result is the seeded draw. Either `seeds` lists them, or `count` seeds
`base_seed, base_seed + 1, …` are used (`base_seed` defaults to `base.seed`). The seed
drives only the stochastic order-latency models (`jitter`, `log_normal`, `heavy_tail`);
under `constant` latency every seed gives the same result. Nothing is selected, so
`cscv_blocks` does not apply.

SweepDesign.description: How the configurations of a sweep are chosen.

SweepProgress.description: Counts over the sweep's runs (a partitioned cell has two).

runs_total.description: Runs planned: one per cell, or in-sample and out-of-sample per cell.

SweepReport.description: The registry report of one sweep.

oneOf.description: `None` when no cell has an in-sample value.

SweepReportCell.description: A configuration as analysed: its parameters and objective values.

in_sample.description: Objective on the selection data: the in-sample window, or the whole dataset.

SweepReportResponse.description:
`GET /sweeps/{id}/report`: the analysis of a finished sweep. Grid and random designs carry
`analysis` (selection, IS→OOS degradation, Spearman, PBO, caveats); a seeds design carries
`ensemble` (per-metric dispersion over seeds) instead.

SweepRequestSpec.description:
The sweep to run: a `SweepSpec` (has `design`), or a legacy two-axis `GridSpec` (has `x` and
`y`), which is converted to a grid sweep on the whole dataset ranked by net P&L.

cscv_blocks.description:
Number of equal time blocks of the selection window (in-sample, or the whole dataset) for
the CSCV probability of backtest overfitting. `None` skips it.

objective.description: Ranks the cells; defaults to maximising net P&L. A seeds ensemble ranks nothing.

oneOf.description:
Without a partition every cell runs once on the whole dataset and no out-of-sample value
exists.

created.description:
`false` when the same spec was already submitted in this workspace (idempotent; any
run missing from an interrupted submission is submitted now).

Tif.description:
Time in force. Semantics are the pinned engine's:
* `Gtc`: rests until filled or cancelled; if it crosses on arrival it takes liquidity.
* `Gtx`: post-only; if it would cross on arrival the exchange model expires it.
* `Ioc`: executes what it can on arrival, remainder expires.
* `Fok`: executes fully on arrival or expires.

TimeWindow.description: Half-open exchange-clock interval `[start, end)`, nanoseconds relative to the dataset origin.

input_unit.description: Unit the source file declared or was told to use.

local_ts_shift_ns.description:
Constant added to all local timestamps during conversion because the source contained
events whose local time preceded their exchange time (clock skew). Zero when none was
needed. Mirrors the reference converter's `correct_local_timestamp`.

TimingSummary.description:
Timing deltas summarised over every pair present in both runs with the same decision (all
classes except `different_decision`, `only_a` and `only_b`), identical pairs included.

max_position.description: Stop quoting the side that would grow `|position|` beyond this.

offset_ticks.description: Quote this many ticks behind the touch (0 joins the best price).

skew_ticks_per_unit.description:
Shift both quotes by `-skew_ticks_per_unit * position` ticks (rounded), so inventory
pushes quotes toward flattening.

side.description: Aggressor side when the data states it.

TruncatedBy.description: Why a page ended before the end of the data.

Value.description: A value always carries its units and contributing/excluded observation counts.

Verdict.description: Machine-readable conclusion. Exactly one applies to an order.
